I was trying to prove something in category theory (equality of some functors), and I kept getting stuck at an HEq goal. I think I have a suitable MWE for the state I am at:

structure Q (n : Nat) : Type where
  data : String

-- Delete one and prove the other

example : Q 1 = Q 2 → @Q.mk 1 "data" ≍ @Q.mk 2 "data" := by sorry

example : ¬ (Q 1 = Q 2 → @Q.mk 1 "data" ≍ @Q.mk 2 "data") := by sorry

Could someone please help resolve this issue by showing which one is the correct one and proving it?

[NOTE : Updated version of the puzzle down below]
Neither of them is provable
@Yaël Dillies Could you please elaborate?
If we assume the two types are equal, we only know that there is a bijection between them, but we don't know how it looks like. It might map "data" to "data" or maybe not.

@Alexander Bentkamp But if that is so, then we should theoretically be able to produce a bijection h : Q 1 = Q 2 which does not map "data" to "data", and since that h is the only evidence we have that Q 1 = Q 2, we can use the fact that its cast will not send @Q.mk 1 "data" to @Q.mk 2 "data", and therefore, we could prove the second example.

I think I can refine my problem, by requiring that the HEq goal be met through the cast given by h : Q 1 = Q 2:

structure Q (n : Nat) : Type where
    data : String

 -- Delete one and prove the other
example : (h : Q 1 = Q 2) → h ▸ @Q.mk 1 "data" = @Q.mk 2 "data" := by sorry

example : ¬ ((h : Q 1 = Q 2) → h ▸ @Q.mk 1 "data" = @Q.mk 2 "data") := by sorry

Thanks for putting this into a MWE, but maybe it would be helpful to post the original theorem that led to needing HEq to see if there is a way to avoid equality of types (e.g. maybe equality of functors is the wrong notion, and natural isomorphism should be preferred, but it might not work in all scenarios).
@Niels Voss We are trying to prove (from scratch) that the category of categories is cartesian closed, here is the code. Cat.exp.proof_unique is where we are stuck at.
I think you might be fine given enough extensionality lemmas for Hom Func

...or maybe curry; lemme poke around a bit.

copy-paste of the code gist

namespace CategoryTheory

  structure Category.{u_1, u_2} : Type (max u_1 u_2 + 1) where
    Obj : Type u_1
    Hom : Obj → Obj → Type u_2
    seq {X Y Z : Obj} : Hom X Y → Hom Y Z → Hom X Z
    assoc {W X Y Z : Obj} {f : Hom W X} {g : Hom X Y} {h: Hom Y Z}
      : seq (seq f g) h = seq f (seq g h)
    id {X : Obj} : Hom X X
    id_left  {X Y : Obj} (f : Hom X Y) : f = seq id f
    id_right {X Y : Obj} (f : Hom X Y) : f = seq f  id

  infixr : 60 " ⟶ " => Category.Hom _
  infixl : 70 " ▷ " => Category.seq _
  notation "𝟙" => Category.id _
  notation "𝟙▷" => Category.id_left _
  notation "▷𝟙" => Category.id_right _

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  structure Terminal.{u_1, u_2} {𝓒 : Category.{u_1, u_2}} : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    obj : 𝓒.Obj
    unique_from (X : 𝓒.Obj) : X ⟶ obj
    proof_unique {X : 𝓒.Obj} : ∀ f : X ⟶ obj, f = unique_from X

  structure Product.{u_1, u_2} {𝓒 : Category.{u_1, u_2}} (A B : 𝓒.Obj) : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    obj : 𝓒.Obj
    fst : obj ⟶ A
    snd : obj ⟶ B
    pair {X : 𝓒.Obj} : X ⟶ A → X ⟶ B → X ⟶ obj
    proof_exists {X : 𝓒.Obj} :
      ∀ fa : X ⟶ A, ∀ fb,
        pair fa fb ▷ fst = fa ∧ pair fa fb ▷ snd = fb
    proof_unique {X : 𝓒.Obj} : ∀ g : X ⟶ obj,
        g = pair (g ▷ fst) (g ▷ snd)

  infixr : 80 " × " => Product
  notation "_fst" => Product.fst _
  notation "_snd" => Product.snd _
  notation "⟨"f", "g"⟩"  => Product.pair _ f g

  def times.{u_1, u_2} {𝓒 : Category.{u_1, u_2}}
    {D D' C C' : 𝓒.Obj}
    {Prod_of_Ds : D × D'}
    {Prod_of_Cs : C × C'}
    (f : D ⟶ C) (f' : D' ⟶ C')
    : Prod_of_Ds.obj ⟶ Prod_of_Cs.obj :=
      ⟨_fst ▷ f, _snd ▷ f'⟩

  infixl : 80 " × " => times

  structure Exponential.{u_1, u_2} {𝓒 : Category.{u_1, u_2}} (A B : 𝓒.Obj) : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    obj : 𝓒.Obj
    any_product : (X : 𝓒.Obj) → X × A
    curry {X : 𝓒.Obj} : (any_product X).obj ⟶ B → X ⟶ obj
    eval : (any_product obj).obj ⟶ B
    proof_exists {X : 𝓒.Obj} :
      ∀ f : (any_product X).obj ⟶ B ,
        (curry f × 𝟙) ▷ eval = f
    proof_unique {X : 𝓒.Obj} :
      ∀ g : X ⟶ obj ,
        g = curry ((g × 𝟙) ▷ eval)

  @[ext]
  structure Func.{u_1, u_2} (𝓐 𝓑 : Category.{u_1, u_2}) : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    Obj : 𝓐.Obj → 𝓑.Obj
    Mor {X Y : 𝓐.Obj} : X ⟶ Y → Obj X ⟶ Obj Y
    proof_id {X : 𝓐.Obj} : Mor (@𝓐.id X) = 𝟙
    proof_comp {X Y Z : 𝓐.Obj} :
      ∀ (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), Mor (f ▷ g) = Mor f ▷ Mor g

  structure NatTransform.{u_1, u_2} {𝓐 𝓑 : Category.{u_1, u_2}} (F G : Func 𝓐 𝓑) : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    component : (a : 𝓐.Obj) → F.Obj a ⟶ G.Obj a
    proof {X Y : 𝓐.Obj} :
      ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, F.Mor f ▷ component Y = component X ▷ G.Mor f

  structure CartesianClosedCategory.{u_1, u_2} (𝓒 : Category.{u_1, u_2}) : Type (max u_1 u_2) where
    terminal : @Terminal 𝓒
    prod (A B : 𝓒.Obj) : Product A B
    exp  (A B : 𝓒.Obj) : Exponential A B

end CategoryTheory



namespace CategoryOfCategories

  open CategoryTheory

  -- TODO : Switch direction of things like Functor.proof, 𝟙▷, ▷𝟙

  def seq.{u} {𝓧 𝓨 𝓩 : Category.{u, u}} : Func 𝓧 𝓨 → Func 𝓨 𝓩 → Func 𝓧 𝓩 := fun F G =>
    {
      Obj := G.Obj ∘ F.Obj
      Mor := G.Mor ∘ F.Mor
      proof_id := by
        simp [F.proof_id, G.proof_id]
      proof_comp := by
        intro _ _ _ f g
        have h2 := G.proof_comp (F.Mor f) (F.Mor g)
        rw [← (F.proof_comp f g)] at h2
        exact h2
    }

  /--
    `Cat.{u}` is the category of all `Category.{u, u}` categories.
  -/
  def Cat.{u} : Category.{u + 1, u} :=
    have assoc := by simp [seq]; exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    let id {𝓧 : Category} : Func 𝓧 𝓧 := .mk id id (by simp) (fun _ _ => rfl)
    have id_left  := by simp [seq]
    have id_right := by simp [seq]
    .mk Category.{u, u} Func seq assoc id id_left id_right

  def Cat.terminal.{u} : Terminal (𝓒 := Cat.{u}) := {
    obj := {
      Obj := PUnit
      Hom := fun _ _ => PUnit
      seq := fun _ _ => PUnit.unit
      assoc := fun {W X Y Z} {f g h} => PUnit.eq_punit PUnit.unit
      id := PUnit.unit
      id_left := by simp only [implies_true]
      id_right := by simp only [implies_true]
    }
    unique_from := fun _ => {
      Obj := fun _ => PUnit.unit
      Mor := fun _ => PUnit.unit
      proof_id := by simp only [implies_true]
      proof_comp := by simp only [implies_true]
    }
    proof_unique := by intros; rfl
  }

  def Cat.prod.{u} (𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj) : 𝓐 × 𝓑 := {
    obj := {
      Obj := 𝓐.Obj × 𝓑.Obj
      Hom := fun (w,x) (y,z) => (w ⟶ y) × (x ⟶ z)
      seq := fun a b => (a.fst ▷ b.fst, a.snd ▷ b.snd)
      assoc := by
        simp [𝓐.assoc, 𝓑.assoc]
      id := (𝟙, 𝟙)
      id_left := by simp [← 𝟙▷]
      id_right := by simp [← ▷𝟙]
    }
    fst := {
      Obj := Prod.fst
      Mor := Prod.fst
      proof_id := by simp
      proof_comp := by simp
    }
    snd := {
      Obj := Prod.snd
      Mor := Prod.snd
      proof_id := by simp
      proof_comp := by simp
    }
    pair := fun f g => {
      Obj := fun x => (f.Obj x, g.Obj x)
      Mor := fun x => (f.Mor x, g.Mor x)
      proof_id := by simp [f.proof_id, g.proof_id]
      proof_comp := by simp [f.proof_comp, g.proof_comp]
    }
    proof_exists := by
      intros
      refine And.intro ?_ ?_
      all_goals rfl
    proof_unique := by intros; rfl
  }

  def Cat.exp.obj.{u} (𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj) : Cat.Obj := {
    Obj := Func 𝓐 𝓑
    Hom := fun F G => NatTransform F G
    seq := fun τ₁ τ₂ => {
      component := fun a => τ₁.component a ▷ τ₂.component a
      proof := by
        simp only [𝓑.assoc, ← τ₂.proof]
        simp only [← 𝓑.assoc, τ₁.proof, implies_true]
    }
    assoc := by simp only [𝓑.assoc, implies_true]
    id := {
      component := fun x => 𝟙
      proof := by grind only [𝟙▷, ▷𝟙]
    }
    id_left := by simp only [← 𝟙▷, implies_true]
    id_right := by simp only [← ▷𝟙, implies_true]
  }

  def Cat.exp.curry.{u} {𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj} {𝓧 : Cat.Obj} :
    Cat.Hom (prod 𝓧 𝓐).obj 𝓑 → Cat.Hom 𝓧 (obj 𝓐 𝓑) := fun F =>
      let h := @F.proof_id
      {
        Obj := fun x => {
          Obj := fun a => F.Obj (x, a)
          Mor := fun f => F.Mor (𝟙, f)
          proof_id := by
            simp [prod] at h
            simp [h]
          proof_comp := by simp only [prod, ← F.proof_comp, ← 𝟙▷, implies_true]
        }
        Mor := fun f => {
          component := fun _ => F.Mor (f, 𝟙)
          proof := by simp only [prod, ← F.proof_comp, ← 𝟙▷, ← ▷𝟙, implies_true]
        }
        proof_id := by
          simp [prod] at h
          simp [h, obj]
        proof_comp := by simp only [prod, ← F.proof_comp, ← 𝟙▷, implies_true, obj]
      }

  def Cat.exp.eval.{u} {𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj} :
    Cat.Hom (prod (obj 𝓐 𝓑) 𝓐).obj 𝓑 := {
      Obj := fun p => p.fst.Obj p.snd
      Mor := @fun p q r => p.fst.Mor r.snd ▷ r.fst.component q.snd
      proof_id := by
        simp [prod, Func.proof_id, ← 𝟙▷, obj]
      proof_comp := by
        simp only [prod, Prod.forall, obj]
        intros; expose_names
        rw [a.proof_comp]
        have h1 := a_3.proof b_4
        rw [𝓑.assoc]
        conv in 𝓑.seq (a.Mor b_4) _ => rw [←𝓑.assoc, h1]
        repeat rw [𝓑.assoc]
    }

  def Cat.exp.proof_exists.{u} {𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj} :
    ∀ {𝓧 : Cat.Obj} (F : Cat.Hom (prod 𝓧 𝓐).obj 𝓑), seq (curry F × Cat.id) eval = F := by
      intro 𝓧 F
      ext
      all_goals simp [seq, eval, curry, prod, times, Cat]
      . congr 1
      . ext
        simp [← F.proof_comp, prod, ← 𝟙▷, ← ▷𝟙]

  def Cat.exp.proof_unique.{u} {𝓐 𝓑 : Cat.{u}.Obj} :
    ∀ {𝓧 : Cat.Obj} (G : Cat.Hom 𝓧 (obj 𝓐 𝓑)), G = curry (seq (G × Cat.id) eval) := by
      sorry

  /--
  For any `u`, the category of all `Category.{u, u}` categories is cartesian closed.
  -/
  def Cat_is_CC.{u} : CartesianClosedCategory Cat.{u} :=
    {
      terminal := Cat.terminal
      prod := Cat.prod
      exp := fun 𝓐 𝓑 => {
        obj := Cat.exp.obj 𝓐 𝓑
        any_product := fun 𝓧 => Cat.prod 𝓧 𝓐
        curry := Cat.exp.curry
        eval := Cat.exp.eval
        proof_exists := Cat.exp.proof_exists
        proof_unique := Cat.exp.proof_unique
      }
    }

end CategoryOfCategories

structure Q (n : Nat) : Type where
  data : String

example : Q 1 = Q 2 → @Q.mk 1 "data" ≍ @Q.mk 2 "data" := by sorry

example : ¬ (Q 1 = Q 2 → @Q.mk 1 "data" ≍ @Q.mk 2 "data") := by sorry

-- this gives you a `Q : Nat → Type`, a `Q.mk : {n : Nat} → String → Q n`,
-- and a `Q.rec.{u} : {n : Nat} → {motive : Q n → Sort u} → ((data : String) → motive (Q.mk data)) → (t : Q n) → motive t`
-- which satisfies the definitional equality `Q.rec mk (Q.mk data) = mk data`

-- so if we can provide our own `MyQ`, `MyQ.mk`, `MyQ.rec`, which satisfies the same equality propositionally,
-- then every theorem provable for `Q` should be provable for `MyQ` as well

def MyQ1 (n : Nat) : Type := String
def MyQ1.mk {n : Nat} (data : String) : MyQ1 n := data
def MyQ1.rec.{u} {n : Nat} {motive : MyQ1 n → Sort u}
    (mk : (data : String) → motive (MyQ1.mk data)) (t : MyQ1 n) : motive t :=
  mk t
theorem MyQ1.rec_mk.{u} {n : Nat} {motive : MyQ1 n → Sort u} (mk : (data : String) → motive (MyQ1.mk data)) (data : String) :
    @MyQ1.rec n motive mk (MyQ1.mk data) = mk data := by rfl

-- it is consistent with Lean that the first example is true, so the second example is unprovable
example : MyQ1 1 = MyQ1 2 → @MyQ1.mk 1 "data" ≍ @MyQ1.mk 2 "data" := by intro; rfl

opaque String.reverse : {f : String → String // (∀ x, f (f x) = x) ∧ f "data" ≠ "data"} :=
  ⟨fun x => String.ofList x.toList.reverse, by simp⟩

def MyQ2 (n : Nat) : Type := String
def MyQ2.mk {n : Nat} (data : String) : MyQ2 n :=
  if n = 1 then
    String.reverse.1 data
  else data
def MyQ2.rec.{u} {n : Nat} {motive : MyQ2 n → Sort u}
    (mk : (data : String) → motive (MyQ2.mk data)) (t : MyQ2 n) : motive t :=
  if h : n = 1 then
    Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x) (mk (String.reverse.1 t)) ?h1
  else
    Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x) (mk t) ?h2
where finally
  case h1 =>
    unfold MyQ2 MyQ2.mk
    simp [h, String.reverse.2.1]
  case h2 =>
    unfold MyQ2 MyQ2.mk
    simp [h]
theorem MyQ2.rec_mk.{u} {n : Nat} {motive : MyQ2 n → Sort u} (mk : (data : String) → motive (MyQ2.mk data)) (data : String) :
    @MyQ2.rec n motive mk (MyQ2.mk data) = mk data := by
  have pf1 (h : n = 1) (t : MyQ2 n) : MyQ2.mk (String.reverse.val t) = t := by
    unfold MyQ2 MyQ2.mk
    simp [h, String.reverse.2.1]
  have pf2 (h : ¬n = 1) (t : MyQ2 n) : MyQ2.mk t = t := by
    unfold MyQ2 MyQ2.mk
    simp [h]
  have e1 (hn : n = 1) : @MyQ2.mk n = String.reverse.1 := by
    unfold MyQ2.mk MyQ2
    simp [hn]
  have e2 (hn : ¬n = 1) : @MyQ2.mk n = @id String := by
    unfold MyQ2.mk MyQ2
    simp [hn, funext_iff]
  unfold MyQ2.rec at *
  split <;> rename_i h
  · change Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x) _ (pf1 h (MyQ2.mk data)) = mk data
    revert mk pf1 pf2
    rw [e1 h]
    intro mk pf1 pf2
    refine Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x)
      (mk x) (congrArg String.reverse.1 h.symm) = mk data) ?_ (pf1 h data).symm
    rfl
  · change Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x) _ (pf2 h (MyQ2.mk data)) = mk data
    revert mk pf1 pf2
    rw [e2 h]
    intro mk pf1 pf2
    refine Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => Eq.rec (motive := fun x h => motive x)
      (mk x) h.symm = mk data) ?_ (pf2 h data).symm
    rfl

-- it is consistent with Lean that the second example is true, so the first example is unprovable
example : ¬ (MyQ2 1 = MyQ2 2 → @MyQ2.mk 1 "data" ≍ @MyQ2.mk 2 "data") := by
  intro h
  exact String.reverse.2.2 (eq_of_heq (h rfl))
